title: Circuit encoding belongs to the inner language
statement: Let $d$ be a refutation data package and let $L_2,K$ be languages of Boolean strings. Suppose that for every string $y$, membership in $L_2$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $v$ with $|v|=M_2(y)$ and $\langle y,v\rangle\in K$. Suppose that for every string $z$, nonmembership in $K$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $r$ with $|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ and $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$. Let $m\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $D_n$ be a directed acyclic circuit on $n+m(n)$ input bits for every $n$, each with fan-in at most two; assume that $z\in K$ exactly when some assignment to its last $m(|z|)$ input bits makes $D_{|z|}$ accept $z$ concatenated with that assignment. Suppose that for all Boolean strings $x,U,u,v,w,r$ with $|u|=M_1(x)$, $|v|\le M_2(\langle x,u\rangle)$, $|w|\le|U|$, and $|r|\le C_3(nLen(x)+1)^{c_3}$, one has $|\langle\langle u,v\rangle,\langle w,r\rangle\rangle|\le B(|\langle x,U\rangle|+1)^b$. If every string $u$ of length $M_1(x)$ satisfies $\langle x,u\rangle\in L_2$, then $\langle x,D_{nLen(x)}.encode\rangle$ belongs to the inner language.
hypotheses_covered: For every $y$, $y\in L_2$ iff there exists $v$ with $|v|=M_2(y)$ and $\langle y,v\rangle\in K$
For every $z$, $z\notin K$ iff there exists $r$ with $|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ and $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$
For every $n$, $D_n$ is a circuit on $n+m(n)$ input bits
Every $D_n$ has fan-in at most two

The stated length bound holds for all $x,U,u,v,w,r$ satisfying the four listed length constraints

replaced:
Let $d$ be a data record with parameters $C_1,c_1,C_2,c_2,C_3,c_3,B,b$ and refutation
relation $R$, and let $L_2,K$ be languages of binary strings. Suppose membership in
$L_2$ is equivalent to having a certificate $v$ of length $M_2(y)$ with $\langle
y,v\rangle\in K$, and membership in the complement of $K$ is equivalent to having a
refutation $r$ of length at most $C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ with $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$.
Suppose also that for every input length $n$ there is a fan-in-two circuit $D_n$ on
$n+m(n)$ input bits, and that $z\in K$ exactly when some assignment to its last $m(|z|)$
input bits makes $D_{|z|}$ accept the concatenation of $z$ with that assignment. Assume
that whenever $|v|\le C_2(2|x|+2+M_1(x)+1)^{c_2}$ and $|w|\le |U|$, the encoding
$\langle v,w\rangle$ has length at most $B(|\langle\langle x,U\rangle,t\rangle|+1)^b$.
If every string $u$ of length $M_1(x)$ satisfies $\langle x,u\rangle\in L_2$, then
$\langle x,D_{nLen(x)}.encode\rangle$ belongs to the inner language: for every string
$t$, the string obtained by pairing it with $\langle x,D_{nLen(x)}.encode\rangle$ fails
the bad-language condition.
